I confirmed the figures against the records the route census names, as the task asked. THE $200: the packet says 'The circuit clerk charges the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee, which the official text sets at $200.' The committed track registry's wv_conv_single_misdemeanor destination.detail says 'paying the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee, which the official text sets at $200', the committed route census carries the same sentence on this route key, and the committed packet-set manifest's pay_fee entry says the same. Any relief from the $200 circuit clerk fee would be under the circuit court's ordinary civil indigency practice, which the controlling review did not establish.' A3 holds that a record establishes an answer only for the route it actually addresses, and that a line keyed to a different statutory section is a sibling-route inference A2 already forbids. Run on this route's fee fact — the circuit clerk's charge for a § 61-11-26 misdemeanour conviction expungement petition — the test comes out clean, and it shows the repair dodged a live trap of exactly A3's shape. THE RECORDS THAT DO ADDRESS THIS ROUTE: the track registry entry is keyed by trackId to this track, the route census entry is keyed by the full route key, and the packet-set manifest entry is keyed by packetSetId; all three carry the § 59-1-11(a)(1) $200 sentence for this route and nothing else. SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Two things fail together and the second is the serious one. First, structurally: the packet has no "when to stop and get help" section at all, on either the guidance page or in participant-instructions.md, and none of the registry's three selfHelpStopConditions is carried as a stop. The participant has not yet obtained a pardon, which the registry says is out of scope and a referral, is nowhere. Whether the pardon is conditional or unconditional cannot be determined from the document is reduced to a description of the difference between the two. The record still appears after the quarterly cycle and the fallback route's availability is unclear is not carried as a stop. Second, and this is a DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A4 violation on the delivered bytes: the guidance page, packet pages 4-5 of both fixtures, tells the participant "This page states no timetable and no criterion for that, because neither is established by the two forms this packet is built from, and an unsourced criterion in a filing instruction is worse than none." The timetable IS established, for this exact route, in three committed records I read at this base. The track registry's packetInstructions for pa_pardon_expungement says "Tell the participant a pardon does not by itself erase the record, and that the Board transmits eligible records to the AOPC quarterly." Its manualCompletionItems carry "Quarterly verification date — Guidance, verification schedule — The participant records when they checked whether the automatic route cleared the record", listed as required before filing. Its packetSet condition on the petition component reads "Generated only where the automatic route has not cleared the record after the quarterly cycle." And src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/PA-pennsylvania.json states "the Board of Pardons transmits eligible records to AOPC quarterly, AOPC sends the record to the court of common pleas, and the court orders expungement after confirming the criteria." The same packet states the quarterly cycle on another page — participant-instructions.md paragraph 4 says the Board transmits eligible records to the AOPC quarterly, in bold. So the packet tells the participant, on the page that goes in the envelope, that it does not state something it states on the page that does not. The guidance page compounds it by narrowing its own source universe to "the two forms this packet is built from", which is precisely the narrowing A2 forbids: the repository's committed records are held sources, not just the PDFs. The registry's named verification schedule is absent from the guidance page in consequence.

whyTheseAreNotRows.what: These eight refusals are recorded here and NOT appended to the rows array, deliberately.
whyTheseAreNotRows.why: extract-verifier-returns.mjs reads every entry in rows as a verdict ABOUT THE FAMILY and keeps one current verdict per family. Its supersedes() prefers a row whose declared verifiedAtBase is a descendant of the incumbent's. All eight of these families currently carry FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED at bases 7fcfb7d40aafe7bd7350fc735ea09d16524cb757, ebc44031ec7eab29058bfc79a7bc5e1cff089414 and 36d7718a7e48d7f87f18eeaf3b18ed9b3ce545c8; git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms each is an ancestor of this base. A row of mine declaring this base would therefore have superseded all eight.
whyTheseAreNotRows.measuredConsequence: The baseline sweep at this base reports 32 FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED families and names all eight of these among them. Appending these refusals as rows would have taken that list to 24 — eight known-failing families dropped off the repair queue on the strength of a read that never happened, replaced by a verdict that is a statement about this lane rather than about the packet.
whyTheseAreNotRows.therefore: A claim-gate refusal is not a verdict about a family and is not recorded as one. rows is left exactly as the previous lanes wrote it; nothing was superseded, upgraded, downgraded or removed.
whyTheseAreNotRows.aStructuralFindingForCaptain: The extractor has no way to say 'this lane could not look'. Its vocabulary contains BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM and STOPPED, but any row carrying them still competes for the family's single current-verdict slot and still displaces an actionable FAIL. If refused lanes are expected to return rows, the extractor should exclude non-reading verdicts from supersession. Raised, not decided, and not repaired here: this lane may not edit factory scripts.
whyTheseAreNotRows.alsoChecked: All fifteen obligation names already appear in each of these four documents, so adding them here leaves unscoredObligations empty as it already was, and no other lane's PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT row changes its downgrade state.
